item.content:encoded:
Living in Redstone: Calgary's Welcoming NE Community

Redstone is one of northeast Calgary's most thoughtfully designed master-planned communities, offering modern homes, abundant green space, and a genuinely diverse and welcoming atmosphere. Developed through the 2010s and continuing into the 2020s along the northeast ring road corridor, Redstone Calgary homes attract young families, first-time buyers, and newcomers seeking contemporary suburban living at accessible price points. Whether you are searching for a starter townhome or a spacious six-bedroom detached house, Redstone delivers outstanding value in a community built from the ground up with residents in mind. Raman Basra and the team at ramanbasra.ca have helped many clients find their perfect home in this thriving northeast neighbourhood—and there has never been a better time to explore what Redstone has to offer.

Location & Getting Around

Redstone sits in Calgary's northeast quadrant, bordered by Stoney Trail to the west and Metis Trail running through the heart of the community. This prime position provides effortless access to the city's ring road network, making commutes across Calgary swift and straightforward. The Calgary International Airport is only minutes away—a huge draw for frequent flyers and airline employees. The community is well-served by the Calgary Transit system, with bus routes connecting residents to major transit hubs and the CTrain network. Stoney Trail links directly to Deerfoot Trail in minutes, putting downtown Calgary within a 25-to-30-minute drive on most days.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

Redstone is proudly one of Calgary's most multicultural neighbourhoods. Neighbours from diverse cultures, traditions, and backgrounds come together here, creating an inclusive and vibrant community spirit that residents consistently praise. The streets are quiet and family-oriented, with wide sidewalks, well-lit pathways, and a pace of life designed for people raising children or simply enjoying a relaxed suburban existence. Community engagement is strong: local social media groups buzz with events, seasonal gatherings, and neighbour-to-neighbour connections that give Redstone a small-town warmth within a growing city. Over 3.5 km of winding pathways thread through the neighbourhood, connecting parks, schools, and open green space—perfect for morning runs, evening walks, or weekend bike rides. The Partici-Park features adult-sized outdoor fitness equipment alongside a children's playground and basketball court, keeping residents of all ages active year-round.

Schools & Education

Families in Redstone are well-served by both the Calgary Board of Education (CBE) and the Calgary Catholic School District (CSSD). Public school options in and near the community include Keeler School (elementary), Dr. Gordon Higgins Junior High School, and James Fowler High School. Catholic families can access St. Isidore School, St. John XXIII School, and Bishop McNally High School. The community master plan also includes two future school sites—both an elementary and a high school—earmarked for construction within Redstone itself, ensuring that as the neighbourhood grows, its youngest residents will have education options steps from their front door.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

Green space is woven into Redstone's DNA. Redstone Park serves as a central hub for family recreation, featuring playgrounds designed for children of all ages. The community's Partici-Park is a neighbourhood standout, offering an outdoor circuit training area alongside basketball courts—rare in newer suburban developments. Just beyond Redstone's borders lies the Nose Creek Parkway, a sprawling 73-hectare natural area with extensive walking and cycling trails, picnic tables, and wildlife habitat that gives residents a genuine nature escape without leaving northeast Calgary. For indoor recreation, the Genesis Centre—a 255,000-square-foot community hub located just a short drive away—is home to a YMCA fitness centre, a Calgary Public Library branch, two indoor fieldhouses, outdoor soccer fields, a 30,000-square-foot gymnasium, a community kitchen, and a full event hall, making it one of the finest recreational facilities in the city.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Daily conveniences are well within reach for Redstone residents. The community's own Redstone Market Square hosts a No Frills grocery store and a Shoppers Drug Mart, covering everyday essentials without leaving the neighbourhood. For larger shopping runs, CrossIron Mills—one of Alberta's largest outlet shopping centres with over 200 stores—is a short drive up Stoney Trail. A Costco is also conveniently nearby. Dozens of restaurants, cafés, and specialty shops dot the surrounding northeast area along Country Hills Boulevard and Airport Trail, giving Redstone residents a wide range of dining and retail options. The proximity to the airport also means that hotel amenities, car rental services, and international-level dining experiences are all within a 10-minute drive.

Real Estate in Redstone

Redstone offers one of the most diverse housing stocks in northeast Calgary, catering to a broad spectrum of budgets and family sizes. The community's housing mix includes detached single-family homes, semi-detached properties, and townhomes—all predominantly built over the past decade and featuring modern open-concept layouts, nine-foot ceilings, energy-efficient construction, and contemporary finishes.

As of mid-2026, the average listed price across all Redstone home types sits at approximately $535,000, with a median of around $486,000. Townhomes represent the most accessible entry point, with average sold prices around $396,000 over the past year—a compelling value proposition for first-time buyers priced out of the city's west or south communities. Larger detached homes, particularly those with legal suites or five-plus bedrooms, range from the upper $600,000s into the $900,000-plus range for premium builds.

The current market in Redstone reflects broader conditions across Calgary in 2026: inventory has risen, giving buyers more selection and negotiating room than they enjoyed in the frenzied 2022–2024 period. Homes are taking somewhat longer to sell, and sale-to-list price ratios have eased slightly, meaning well-prepared buyers can find excellent deals on move-in-ready properties. For investors, the northeast's sustained population growth—driven in part by immigration and proximity to the airport employment corridor—continues to support healthy long-term rental demand. Working with an experienced local agent like Raman Basra ensures you have the market intelligence to act confidently in this evolving environment.

Why Choose Redstone?

  • Outstanding value for new construction: Modern homes with premium finishes at price points well below comparable product on Calgary's west or south sides.
  • Diverse, welcoming community: One of Calgary's most multicultural neighbourhoods, known for its inclusive atmosphere and strong community bonds.
  • Exceptional connectivity: Direct Stoney Trail and Deerfoot Trail access, proximity to the airport, and solid transit links make getting around the city effortless.
  • World-class recreation nearby: The Genesis Centre is among the best community recreation facilities in western Canada, available to Redstone residents minutes from home.
  • Buyer-friendly 2026 market: Rising inventory and easing prices mean motivated buyers can negotiate well and secure a home that fits their needs and budget.

Start Your Redstone Home Search Today

Redstone is a community that delivers on every level—modern design, family-friendly living, strong amenities, and real value in Calgary's dynamic real estate market. Whether you are buying your first home, upsizing for a growing family, or adding a rental property to your portfolio, Redstone belongs on your shortlist. item.title: Valley Ridge: Calgary's Top-Ranked NW Neighbourhood Guide (2026)
item.description: Discover Valley Ridge, Calgary's #1 ranked NW neighbourhood in 2026 with 46% five-year growth, golf course living, Bow River trails & top schools.
item.content:encoded:
Living in Valley Ridge

Valley Ridge is one of Calgary's most acclaimed communities — and in 2026, it officially claimed the top spot as the city's best neighbourhood for real estate investment, boasting a remarkable 46.45% five-year price growth and an average home price of approximately $859,665. Tucked into the western edge of Calgary along the Bow River valley, Valley Ridge feels less like a suburban subdivision and more like a private retreat where escarpment views, emerald fairways, and forested ravines frame everyday life. Whether you're a growing family seeking great schools and safe streets, a nature lover drawn to riverside trails, or a savvy buyer looking for strong long-term value, Valley Ridge Calgary homes consistently deliver. Raman Basra, Calgary's trusted real estate expert, knows this community inside and out — and is ready to help you find your perfect fit here.

Location & Getting Around

Valley Ridge sits in Calgary's northwest (NW) quadrant, bounded by the Bow River to the north and the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 1) to the south, with Stoney Trail forming its eastern edge. This positioning gives residents effortless access to the entire city — downtown Calgary is roughly 20–25 minutes east via the Trans-Canada, while the Rocky Mountains and Cochrane are a short drive west. Bowness Road NW connects neighbours to Bowness Park and the established communities to the east. Calgary Transit bus routes serve the neighbourhood, though like most western communities, Valley Ridge is best navigated by car, making it ideal for families comfortable with a vehicle-centric lifestyle.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

Valley Ridge carries a distinctive character rooted in nature and privacy. Over 50% of the community is dedicated green space — an extraordinary figure even by Calgary's generous standards — and that commitment to open land shapes every aspect of life here. Wildlife sightings (deer, foxes, and birds of prey) are common along the ravine pathways, and the fairways of the Valley Ridge Golf Course wind through the heart of the neighbourhood, lending the entire area a parkland aesthetic. The community skews toward established professionals and families who value quiet cul-de-sacs, large lots, and the peaceful hum of a mature neighbourhood. The Valley Ridge Community Association organizes seasonal events and programming, fostering the tight-knit spirit that newcomers consistently remark on. It's a place where neighbours wave from driveways and kids bike safely in the evenings — a rare quality in a city growing as fast as Calgary.

Schools & Education

Valley Ridge does not have schools within its immediate boundaries, but families have strong options in close proximity. On the Calgary Board of Education (CBE) side, Belvedere-Parkway Elementary School serves younger children, while Thomas P. Riley School covers junior high grades, and Bowness High School is the go-to destination for grades 10–12. Calgary Catholic School District (CSSD) families are served by Our Lady of the Assumption School (K–9), St. Madeleine d'Houet Junior High, and St. Mary's High School for grades 10–12. The commute to each school is manageable, and the quality of instruction across all these institutions draws families specifically to this corner of the city.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

Recreation is woven into the DNA of Valley Ridge. The crown jewel is the Valley Ridge Golf Course, an 18-hole championship layout that winds through the community's natural terrain and is widely regarded as one of Calgary's premier public courses. Beyond the fairways, the Bow River Pathway connects residents directly to Bowness Park and Baker Park — two of Calgary's most beloved green spaces, perfect for picnics, skating in winter, and kayaking in summer. Within the neighbourhood, a soccer pitch, two ball diamonds, and well-maintained playgrounds keep families active year-round. Ravine trails invite hikers and cyclists, and the Bow River itself offers opportunities for fishing and wildlife observation. For those who value outdoor living above all else, Valley Ridge is simply hard to beat.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Valley Ridge has a thoughtful collection of everyday services within the community itself — a gas station, pharmacy, dry cleaner, salon, barbershop, and a few dining spots including the Van Gogh Grill and Bar, CPG Calgary Pizza, and Mulligan's restaurant at the golf course. For full-scale retail, Aspen Landing Shopping Centre is just minutes away and serves as the neighbourhood's main commercial hub, offering groceries, cafes, and specialty shops. A slightly longer drive brings you to Crowfoot Crossing, one of northwest Calgary's largest retail destinations, with over 350 stores, a Cineplex Odeon, YMCA, Starbucks, Shoppers Drug Mart, and virtually every everyday convenience imaginable. Valley Ridge residents trade some walkability for an exceptional sense of seclusion — a trade most here make with zero regrets.

Real Estate in Valley Ridge

Valley Ridge is Calgary's standout performer in 2026. The neighbourhood earned the city's top Economics Score of 5.0 and leads all Calgary communities with 46.45% five-year price growth — a statistic that speaks both to underlying demand and the neighbourhood's enduring desirability. The average home price sits around $859,665, placing it firmly in the upper-middle to luxury segment of the Calgary market.

The housing stock is dominated by large single-family detached homes, typically three to five bedrooms, with attached double garages and generous lot sizes. Styles range from classic two-storey family homes to elegant estate properties with mountain views. Entry-level buyers can find opportunities in the mid-$400,000s for townhomes and smaller detached homes, while luxury estate properties regularly command $1.2M to $1.5M and beyond.

Inventory in Valley Ridge tends to be tight — the community's fixed size, desirable location, and strong demand keep turnover low. Homes are listed and sold quickly when priced well, and multiple-offer situations are not uncommon for move-in-ready properties. For buyers, working with an agent who knows the community is essential. Raman Basra has extensive experience in west Calgary's luxury and family markets and can help you navigate Valley Ridge real estate with confidence, whether you're buying your first home here or upgrading within the community.

Why Choose Valley Ridge?

  • Calgary's #1 investment neighbourhood in 2026 — 46.45% five-year growth and a perfect Economics Score of 5.0 make it the city's top performer for long-term value.
  • Unmatched natural setting — over 50% green space, an 18-hole golf course, Bow River pathways, and ravine trails right on your doorstep.
  • Strong school access — solid CBE and CSSD options within easy reach, including Our Lady of the Assumption (K–9) and Bowness High School.
  • Peaceful, private community feel — mature, established neighbourhood with a tight-knit community association and a lifestyle that prioritizes tranquility and space.
  • Excellent connectivity — quick access to Stoney Trail, Trans-Canada Highway, and downtown Calgary, plus proximity to Cochrane and the Rockies for weekend adventures.

item.title: Shawnee Park: Calgary's Nature-Connected SW Neighbourhood Guide (2026)
item.description: Discover Shawnee Park, Calgary's SW gem beside Fish Creek Park. New homes from $790K, CTrain access & nature trails. 2026 guide by Raman Basra.
item.content:encoded:
Living in Shawnee Park

Tucked into the southwest corner of Calgary, Shawnee Park is one of the city's most exciting new communities — a rare address where nature, connectivity, and modern design come together on the last developable land bordering Fish Creek Provincial Park. Built on the former Shawnee Slopes Golf Course site, this thoughtfully planned neighbourhood by Cardel Homes blends mature green space with contemporary Shawnee Park Calgary homes ranging from stylish townhomes to spacious estate residences. If you're searching for a community that feels established from day one yet offers brand-new construction, Shawnee Park deserves a close look. Raman Basra and his team at ramanbasra.ca know this corner of Calgary well and can help you navigate the market with confidence.

Location & Getting Around

Shawnee Park sits in the deep southwest of Calgary, anchored near James McKevitt Road SW and Macleod Trail. The community's most celebrated transit feature is its immediate access to the Fish Creek–Lacombe CTrain station, which puts downtown Calgary within a 30-minute commute. Macleod Trail connects residents directly to the Ring Road (Stoney Trail/QE2), making it easy to reach the airport, Deerfoot, or the mountains via Highway 22X. For cyclists and pedestrians, over three kilometres of internal pathways connect to the broader Fish Creek Provincial Park trail network, meaning car-free weekends are genuinely possible.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

Shawnee Park attracts a mix of young families, move-up buyers, and downsizers seeking lock-and-leave townhomes — all drawn by one shared value: quality of life. With nearly 600 mature trees woven through the streetscape and 25 percent of the community dedicated to green space, the neighbourhood has a lush, park-like atmosphere unusual for a brand-new build. Pathways link naturally to Fish Creek Provincial Park — Calgary's beloved 13-kilometre urban wilderness — where residents enjoy birdwatching, mountain biking, cross-country skiing, and picnicking year-round. Weekend mornings in Shawnee Park feel quieter than most new suburbs because the park draws residents away from their cars and onto their feet. A strong sense of community is already forming as Phase 3 releases in late 2026 complete the final streetscapes, with coffee meetups, park walks, and Cardel's community events building neighbourly bonds early.

Schools & Education

Families will find solid public and Catholic options close at hand. Samuel W. Shaw School (CBE, K–9) serves the community's younger residents within the immediate area, while the Catholic system is represented by Father Doucet School (CSSD, K–6). For high school, students typically attend Henry Wise Wood High School, which offers strong academic, sports, and arts programming in nearby Haysboro. The CTrain connection also opens up access to specialized programming and charter schools across the city, making Shawnee Park appealing to families with varied educational needs.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

The defining outdoor feature of Shawnee Park is, without question, its direct border with Fish Creek Provincial Park — one of the largest urban parks in Canada at over 13 kilometres long. Residents step off their doorsteps onto pathways leading into the park's forests, Bow River access points, Bebo Grove picnic areas, and the famous Sikome Lake beach. Within the community itself, the internal pathway network spans more than three kilometres, weaving around pocket parks and naturalized wetland areas. CardelRec South (a municipal recreation facility) is minutes away, and the Shawnessy YMCA offers pools, fitness classes, and youth programming just north on Macleod Trail.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Everyday errands are handled with ease thanks to proximity to Shawnessy Village Shopping Centre, one of Calgary's largest suburban retail hubs with over 200 businesses including Walmart Supercenter, Best Buy, Winners, Alberta Co-op, and a broad range of dining options from quick-service to sit-down restaurants. Shawnessy's commercial strip along Macleod Trail also hosts coffee shops, medical clinics, pharmacies, and specialty grocery stores within a five-minute drive. For entertainment, Landmark Cinemas Shawnessy is nearby, and the Fish Creek–Lacombe CTrain station puts the entire length of Calgary's C-Train dining and shopping scene at residents' fingertips without touching a car.

Real Estate in Shawnee Park

Shawnee Park is an exclusively Cardel Homes community, built on the 52-hectare parcel of the former Shawnee Slopes Golf Course. The product mix includes townhomes, bungalows, and two-storey detached homes, most featuring double or triple garages and premium finishes that reflect the community's move-up buyer demographic. Homes are currently selling from $790,000, positioning Shawnee Park firmly in Calgary's upper-tier new-construction segment — comparable to established communities like Cranston Riverstone or Legacy estates, but with the added premium of Fish Creek Park adjacency and CTrain access few communities can match.

Phase 3 — the most park-adjacent homes, backing directly onto Fish Creek — is releasing in late 2026 and represents the final opportunity to buy new construction here. Calgary's overall market has shifted toward balance in 2026, with the citywide benchmark sitting near $569,200 (July 2026, down 2% year-over-year), giving buyers slightly more negotiating room than during the frenzied 2023–2025 seller's market. Detached homes have held up best, declining only 1% year-over-year, which bodes well for the Shawnee Park segment. Long-term, the scarcity factor is significant: once fully built out, no new homes will ever be added adjacent to this stretch of Fish Creek, making Shawnee Park a unique hold-and-appreciate asset in Calgary's southwest.

Resale homes in the adjacent Shawnee Slopes community — established in the 1980s and 1990s — offer another entry point, typically ranging from the mid-$600,000s for semi-detached homes to over $1 million for large estate properties with mature lots backing Fish Creek.

Why Choose Shawnee Park?

  • Unmatched nature access: Direct border with Fish Creek Provincial Park puts 13 km of trails, river access, and urban wilderness at your front door.
  • CTrain connectivity: Fish Creek–Lacombe station is steps away, offering car-free commuting to downtown and beyond.
  • Limited supply: Built on the last developable parcel beside Fish Creek, Shawnee Park is a true one-of-a-kind location — when it's sold out, it's gone.
  • Premium green design: 600+ mature trees, 3+ km of internal pathways, and 25% green space give the community a lush, established feel from day one.
  • Strong long-term value: Scarcity of park-adjacent land in Calgary's SW, combined with LRT access, supports durable appreciation potential.

Ready to Explore Shawnee Park?

item.title: Silverado: Calgary's Family-Friendly SW Neighbourhood Guide (2026)
item.description: Discover Silverado, Calgary's family-friendly SW community. Explore schools, parks, real estate prices, and why buyers love it in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Living in Silverado

Tucked along Calgary's southern edge, Silverado Calgary homes sit within one of the city's most beloved master-planned communities. Framed by sweeping pathway networks, family-focused schools, and the world-renowned Spruce Meadows equestrian facility just minutes away, Silverado offers a rare combination of suburban tranquility and genuine community spirit. Whether you're a first-time buyer looking to plant roots or a growing family ready to upgrade, Silverado delivers the lifestyle you've been searching for. As a trusted Calgary real estate professional, Raman Basra has helped many buyers discover everything this outstanding SW community has to offer — and the numbers speak for themselves: homes here typically sell in under 10 days, a testament to just how much demand there is for Silverado real estate.

Location & Getting Around

Silverado is located in the southwest quadrant of Calgary, positioned south of Stoney Trail and the Spruce Meadows Trail, and east of the Spruce Meadows equestrian grounds. The community is accessible via Macleod Trail SW and Sheriff King Street SW, making it easy to connect to the rest of the city. The ring road (Stoney Trail/22X) puts Downtown Calgary roughly 30–35 minutes away by car and puts the Calgary International Airport within a reasonable commute. The Somerset–Bridlewood CTrain Station on the Red Line is a short drive north, opening up transit options for daily commuters who prefer to leave the car at home.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

Silverado is a community that genuinely feels like a neighbourhood in the best sense of the word. The streets are quiet, the parks are well-maintained, and residents look out for one another. The Silverado Community Association is the heartbeat of the area, organizing popular events throughout the year including parade of garage sales, Stampede barbecues, movie nights, and seasonal runs — with community memberships available for just $25, offering free entry to many events and local discounts. Next door, Spruce Meadows raises the lifestyle bar considerably: one of the world's premier show jumping and equestrian facilities, it hosts horse shows, trade shows, and the beloved Spruce Meadows International Christmas Market — a magical seasonal tradition that draws visitors from across the city. For everyday recreation, the community's interconnected pathway system winds through green spaces and parks, making it easy to enjoy an evening walk, a morning jog, or a family bike ride right from your front door.

Schools & Education

Families with children will find Silverado exceptionally well served by its school options. Ron Southern School is the neighbourhood's Calgary Board of Education (CBE) elementary school, offering strong academics in a welcoming environment. Catholic families are served by Holy Child School, part of the Calgary Catholic School District (CSSD). For secondary education, students attend Dr. E.P. Scarlett High School in nearby Canyon Meadows — a well-established CBE 10–12 school. A new K-6 and 7-12 school complex is also under development at 100 Silverado Drive SW, set to significantly expand educational capacity in the south. This investment in local education makes Silverado an even more compelling choice for families planning ahead.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

Green space is a defining feature of Silverado's design. The community is laced with paved pathways and walking trails that connect parks, playgrounds, and open green areas throughout the neighbourhood, ideal for families with young kids and dog owners alike. Multiple playgrounds and park nodes are scattered throughout the community, ensuring that outdoor space is never far from home. Just outside the community boundary, Spruce Meadows offers 160+ acres of grounds with year-round programming, making it easy to combine a family outing with world-class equestrian entertainment. The broader Fish Creek Provincial Park is also accessible within a short drive, offering extensive trails, wildlife viewing, and picnic areas for those seeking a bigger outdoor escape.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Residents of Silverado enjoy the convenience of the Silverado Marketplace, a 125,000-square-foot suburban shopping centre immediately to the community's north. Anchored by Sobeys and Shoppers Drug Mart, the Marketplace also features Anytime Fitness, Kildare's Ale House, and a range of professional services including medical clinics, dental offices, and financial services. For a broader retail selection, the Shawnessy Shopping Centre and the retail corridor along Macleod Trail SW — featuring Walmart, Home Depot, Cineplex, and dozens of dining options — is only a short drive north. Day-to-day needs are comfortably met without ever leaving the south end.

Real Estate in Silverado

The Silverado real estate market is highly competitive in 2026, reflecting the strong demand that this well-loved SW community consistently attracts. 100% of homes in Silverado sell within 10 days of listing, with 4.8% selling above asking price — both indicators of a seller's market with robust buyer interest.

Detached homes are the dominant product type and remain the most sought-after. Entry-level detached homes start in the low-to-mid $500s, while larger, fully upgraded properties can exceed $800,000 or more depending on size and finishes. The median sold price for all home types in Silverado was $570,000 as of June 2026, slightly below the city-wide detached average of $814K — representing solid value for the community's quality and location.

Townhomes in Silverado offer a more accessible entry point, with average listing prices around $467,000 and a range from approximately $390,000 to $595,000. These are popular with young couples, downsizers, and buyers entering the market for the first time.

Over the trailing twelve months, the median Silverado home sold for $597,202, with homes spending minimal time on market. The community has shown consistent price appreciation in line with Calgary's broader southwest market trends, driven by its desirable location, quality housing stock, and family-friendly reputation. For buyers and investors alike, Silverado represents a sound long-term choice in one of Calgary's most stable real estate corridors.

Why Choose Silverado?

  • Unbeatable SW location — Easy access to Stoney Trail, Macleod Trail, and the Somerset CTrain station, making the rest of Calgary highly accessible.
  • Spruce Meadows on your doorstep — World-class equestrian events, markets, and seasonal programming right next to the neighbourhood — a lifestyle perk few Calgary communities can match.
  • Excellent schools — Ron Southern School (CBE) and Holy Child School (CSSD) serve the community, with new school construction underway to meet growing demand.
  • Strong resale value — With homes selling in under 10 days and consistent price growth, Silverado is a reliable long-term investment.
  • Vibrant community spirit — An active community association, well-maintained parks, and walkable pathways create a genuine neighbourhood feel that residents consistently praise.

item.title: Rocky Ridge: Calgary's Premier NW Family Neighbourhood Guide (2026)
item.description: Discover Rocky Ridge, Calgary's stunning NW community with mountain views, Shane Homes YMCA, top schools, and homes from $268K–$1.1M+.
item.content:encoded:
Living in Rocky Ridge

Perched on the highest ridgeline in northwest Calgary, Rocky Ridge Calgary homes offer something most communities simply cannot match: sweeping panoramic views of the Rocky Mountains paired with a genuine sense of neighbourhood belonging. At over 1,200 metres above sea level, this established NW community blends natural beauty, world-class recreation, and family-friendly infrastructure into one of the city's most sought-after addresses. Whether you're a young family relocating to Calgary, a move-up buyer chasing more space, or an investor looking for long-term appreciation in a proven community, Rocky Ridge delivers on every front. Raman Basra has helped countless buyers find their perfect home in this remarkable corner of the city, and in this guide we cover everything you need to know before making your move.

Location & Getting Around

Rocky Ridge sits in Calgary's extreme northwest quadrant, bordered by Stoney Trail (Ring Road) to the north and Crowchild Trail to the east. This positioning gives residents fast, direct access to the rest of the city without the congestion that plagues many inner communities. Stoney Trail connects drivers to the airport, south Calgary, and the Trans-Canada Highway in minutes, while Crowchild Trail funnels commuters downtown in roughly 25–30 minutes during peak hours. The community is also served by Calgary Transit bus routes that connect to nearby Tuscany C-Train station, making car-free commuting a viable option for downtown workers.

Community Feel & Lifestyle

Rocky Ridge carries the unhurried, outdoorsy energy of a mountain town without sacrificing city conveniences. The neighbourhood attracts a mix of young families, established professionals, and empty nesters drawn by the elevated topography, environmental reserves, and the strong community association that anchors local life. The Rocky Ridge Royal Oak Community Association (RRROCA) organises year-round programming — from outdoor skating in winter to community garden initiatives in summer — keeping neighbours genuinely connected. The community's design deliberately preserves wetlands, wooded ravines, and a ridge-top pathway corridor, so weekday evenings feel more like a nature retreat than a suburban commute. Crime rates here sit consistently below the Calgary average, making Rocky Ridge one of the city's safer family destinations.

Schools & Education

Families with children will find a strong public and Catholic school presence within and immediately surrounding Rocky Ridge. On the public side, Royal Oak School (CBE, K–9) serves the community directly, with North Trail High School handling senior students in the northwest corridor. Catholic families are well served by Maria Goretti Catholic School (CSSD elementary) as the designated feeder for the area, with access to St. Francis High School and other CSSD junior high options nearby. The proximity of multiple school options within a short drive or walk means most families can avoid the long-haul school runs that come with newer communities on the city's outer edges.

Parks, Pathways & Recreation

Rocky Ridge is anchored by one of Calgary's finest recreation assets: the Shane Homes YMCA at Rocky Ridge. This massive facility includes an eight-lane competition pool, a leisure pool with wave system and waterslide, a multi-purpose ice rink, three full gymnasiums, a fitness centre, fitness studios, and a 160-metre indoor running track — all a few minutes from residents' front doors. Outside, the community's pathway network winds through environmentally sensitive wet ponds, wooded areas, and along the ridge itself, connecting seamlessly to Calgary's broader city-wide pathway system. The Rocky Ridge Athletic Complex offers sports fields and courts, while the community association maintains tennis courts, a splash park, a skating rink, and tot lots for younger children.

Shopping, Dining & Conveniences

Day-to-day errands are handled effortlessly by the Rocky Ridge Shopping Centre at 11595 Rockyvalley Drive NW, anchored by the Calgary Co-op Rocky Ridge Food Centre — a full-service grocery open daily from 8 am to 10 pm, with an attached liquor store and a Co-op gas bar and car wash on site. For broader retail, dining, and entertainment, Crowfoot Crossing is a short drive away and offers a cinema, dozens of restaurants, and major retailers. Market Mall and the shops along Shaganappi Trail are also within easy reach, ensuring Rocky Ridge residents are never more than 15 minutes from virtually anything they need.

Real Estate in Rocky Ridge

The Rocky Ridge real estate market in 2026 reflects strong, sustained demand from buyers who prize the community's lifestyle advantages and long-term value. As of mid-2026, there are approximately 42 active listings with an average asking price of $875,309 — a figure that reflects the community's desirability and the premium buyers place on mountain views and direct access to the YMCA and pathway network.

Detached single-family homes make up the bulk of the market and typically range from $600,000 to over $1.1 million, depending on lot size, ridge-facing orientation, and finishing level. Larger estate homes on premium view lots push past the $1 million mark with relative ease.
